title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
layout_note: Two columns: on the right, the full model as a bottom-to-top stack (Input Embedding, LayerNorm, a grey residual-block frame with Time Mixing and Channel Mixing, then a light-blue 'RWKV-LM Head' frame with LayerNorm, Out, Softmax); on the left, the residual block's insides with the Time Mixing and Channel Mixing sub-blocks opened up. The zoom is implied by matching names and the same grey frame, with no connector lines between the columns.
grouping: Light-grey rounded frames for the residual block in both columns; inside the left frame, two darker blue-grey panels titled 'Time Mixing' and 'Channel Mixing' at their top-left. The LM head is a separate light-blue frame with its name written vertically along its left edge.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with dark outlines; fills code role: tan/peach for LayerNorm and R/K/V projections, yellow for the token-shift mu boxes, orange for sigma, salmon for WKV, cyan for Out, green for Softmax, pink for Input Embedding, grey for the collapsed Time/Channel Mixing blocks. Circled-plus for residual adds and circled-times for gating. Thin dark-grey arrows; residual lines run up the frame's left side.
proposed_highlight: The new operators are the saturated colours inside the zoomed panel: the wide salmon 'WKV' box and orange sigma gate in Time Mixing, and the mu token-shift bars, while the surrounding LayerNorms and the right-hand full-model column stay in muted tones.
lesson: Put the full stack and its expanded block side by side at the same height, with the collapsed blocks in plain grey on one side and their saturated internals on the other, so colour marks where the new operators live.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; published at Findings of EMNLP 2023 (remembered, not printed on the arXiv first page). Figure 3 is a second method figure (the model unrolled over three tokens as an RNN, with 'States' and 'Token shift' arrows between columns) and would also suit a card.

arrangement.units: left: the residual block in a light-grey rounded frame, containing two darker blue-grey sub-panels (Time Mixing, Channel Mixing); right: the full model column with the same grey frame holding collapsed Time/Channel Mixing boxes, topped by a light-blue 'RWKV-LM Head' frame
arrangement.inputs_as: a pink 'Input Embedding' box at the bottom of the right column; the left column takes a bare arrow from below
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the head frame ends in 'Output Probabilities' text over the Softmax box
arrangement.shared: the residual block is drawn twice, collapsed on the right and expanded on the left, matched by name and frame style only

taxonomy.task: RNN-style language modelling with transformer-like parallel training

core.what: two towers side by side: on the right the full model (Input Embedding -> LayerNorm -> residual Time Mixing and Channel Mixing -> RWKV-LM head), on the left the same residual block opened to show the R/K/V/WKV and R'/K'/V' internals of each mixing block

relations.form: the left panel repeats the right panel's block with Time Mixing and Channel Mixing as grey tinted sub-panels containing their operations; no connector ties the two
both towers read bottom to top on straight vertical arrows, with LayerNorm before each mixing block
residual lines run up the left side of each tower and rejoin at circled + nodes above each mixing block
inside Time Mixing, σ(R) and WKV meet at a circled ⊗ before Out; in Channel Mixing σ(R') and V' meet at ⊗

channels.colour: fill = operation type: light orange LayerNorm, pale yellow token shift μ, salmon R/K/V projections, orange σ, cyan Out, green Softmax, grey mixing blocks; pink-red marks both the WKV operator and the Input Embedding, so that colour carries two meanings; blue tint = the LM head
channels.shape: all operations are rounded rectangles; circled glyphs = add/multiply
channels.line: solid arrows only; residual paths are the same weight as data paths
channels.frame: grey rounded panel = one repeated block (both towers); grey inner panels = Time/Channel Mixing; blue panel = head

quality.strengths: the WKV operator is the widest, most saturated box in the time-mixing panel; the two towers share bottom-up reading and the same operation colours; residual lines are straight and short
quality.weaknesses: the detail and overview are not tied by connector or matching position; WKV and Input Embedding share the same pink; the right tower draws loop arrows into the left and right sides of Time Mixing whose meaning is not labelled; the token-shift and recurrence that make WKV novel are a single box rather than drawn over time

insights.structure: The expanded residual block (left) and the full model column (right) stand side by side at the same height, each in a light-grey frame, with the LM head as a separate light-blue frame on top of the right column.
insights.data: No tensors or tokens are drawn; inputs and intermediates are single-letter symbol boxes (R, K, V, mu, sigma) and the output is only the text 'Output Probabilities'.
insights.emphasis: Saturated salmon (WKV), orange (sigma) and yellow (mu) fills appear only inside the zoomed Time and Channel Mixing panels, while the collapsed blocks on the right are flat grey.
insights.flow: Both columns read bottom-to-top along a central spine, with residual lines leaving below each LayerNorm, running up the frame's left side and rejoining at a circled-plus.
insights.avoid: Nothing ties the left panel to the right one (no zoom lines or matching tint), so a reader must infer from the names that the left column is the inside of the right column's grey frame.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
